item.title: Joan Lunden reflects on groundbreaking career, new book with former GMA colleague Bill Ritter
item.description: She sat down with our own Bill Ritter, her longtime co-worker, to talk all about it, including her advice for young people starting their careers in the news business and taking a trip down memory lane.

item.title: Pentagon IDs 4 American troops killed in Kuwait
item.description: The Pentagon on Tuesday identified four of the six American troops killed in the opening hours of the war with Iran.

item.title: AccuWeather Forecast: Cloudy skies tomorrow morning with chance of few sprinkles
item.description: Low clouds have been lingering along the coast today. Expect cloudier skies for all areas by morning as a system moves in and it may bring a few sprinkles.

item.title: Residents rally to demand Richmond keep Flock cameras on and extend contract
item.description: "We are concerned about the vulnerability it creates for our businesses. If Richmond does not have these cameras and all the nearby cities do," says Oscar Garcia, President of the 23rd Street Merchant Association.

item.title: Fearing GOP upset, top California Democrat urges lagging candidates for governor to drop out of race
item.description: Fearful that an election quirk could result in heavily Democratic California installing a Republican as its next governor, a top Democrat on Tuesday sent his party's lagging candidates a blunt message: Get out of the race.

item.title: Why can SF still use 'recyclable' plastic bags despite California's new statewide ban?
item.description: California's new plastic bag law went into effect on January 1. It forbids any business from giving away or selling plastic bags, even those deemed "recyclable."

item.title: Suspected prowler allegedly engaged in 'inappropriate behavior,' linked to 6 Oakland incidents: OPD
item.description: Police are looking for a man who has been linked to at least six instances of prowling in East Oakland neighborhoods. In some cases, police accuse the subject of engaging in inappropriate behavior.

item.title: Mayor Lurie orders $100 million in budget cuts; could lead to elimination of up to 500 jobs
item.description: San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie is ordering city departments to cut $100 million in personnel spending which could lead to the elimination of up to 500 jobs.

item.title: Floats for San Francisco Chinese New Year Parade get finishing touches
item.description: Since it's the year of the fire horse, you'll see a lot of horses and fire symbolism on the floats, housed at Pier 19.

item.title: SF Chinese New Year Parade 2026: How to watch ABC7 Eyewitness News live coverage
item.description: Here's how to watch ABC7 Eyewitness News' broadcast of the largest Lunar New Year Celebration outside of Asia.
